title: Incident TL;DR and Integration Action Kit — EU routing spike
content:
TL;DR:
- What: Short-lived routing spike in EU region causing 10–40% increased API latencies and intermittent 429s for some tenants between 2028-08-17T02:10Z and 2028-08-17T03:05Z.
- Impact: Affected requests predominantly from regional edge nodes in eu-west-1; tenant-facing errors were transient, no data loss.
- Current status: Mitigations applied (routing shim and capacity bump); observing stable response times since 03:10Z. Still monitoring.
- Customer action: None required for most integrations. For partners using regional pinning, a one-time configuration toggle may speed recovery if you observe residual 429s — instructions below.

Audience and intent:
- This draft is intended for: status page update + short customer email for tenants with integration-level guidance (webhooks, regional pinning).
- Tone: plain English, concise TL;DR first, technical appendix for engineers at the bottom.

Suggested statuspage copy (short):
[AT 2028-08-17 03:20Z] Issue: Increased latencies and transient 429 responses impacting some EU-hosted inference requests. We identified a routing imbalance between EU edge nodes and applied an interim routing shim and capacity bump. Most requests are operating normally. We will post a closure update after additional monitoring.

Suggested customer email (concise):
Subject: Incident update — temporary EU routing spike (Aug 17)
Hi —
We wanted to let you know about a short-lived networking event in our EU region this morning that caused elevated latencies and intermittent 429s for a subset of requests. We applied a fix and are seeing normal traffic now. No customer data was affected.
If you continue to see increased latency or 429s, please try the verification steps below and reply to this thread.
Thanks,
Avery on behalf of Redwood Ops

Quick verification steps for integrations teams (copy/paste friendly):
1) Check region header in responses (if you record it):
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -i "x-redwood-region"
  Expected: one of "eu-west-1", "eu-central-1". If responses show region from us-east-1 for EU traffic, open a support ticket.
2) Reproduce error sample (if you see 429):
  curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "input":"test ping"}'
  Capture status code and X-Request-Id header and paste into ticket.
3) Temporary workaround for pinned-region customers:
  In your config: remove explicit region pin for 15 minutes (allowing automatic routing) or switch pin to the alternate EU node (eu-central-1).

Root cause (summary for technical readers):
- Sequence: A partial control-plane rollback of an internal routing optimization introduced an imbalance in request distribution to EU edge nodes. A subset of nodes experienced throughput saturation on NPU queues which surfaced as elevated tail latency and backpressure 429s.
- Why it hit now: The rollback coincided with a sudden traffic burst from a large streaming customer in EU, exceeding the previously reduced per-node soft limits.
- No data integrity issues observed. KV cache preservation and request logs are intact.

Mitigation timeline (concise):
- 02:10Z: On-call alerting triggered (latency spike).
- 02:18Z: Ops paged; initial mitigation: reroute traffic away from saturated nodes.
- 02:30Z: Identified control-plane change as likely cause; issued rollback of the rollback to restore optimizer settings.
- 02:45Z: Applied temporary routing shim and increased per-node soft limit (+20%).
- 03:05Z: Error rate dropped to baseline; continuing to monitor.
- 03:20Z: Drafted statuspage + customer note. Postmortem tracking opened.

Customer-facing remediation and credits:
- Eligibility: Tenants who saw >1% error rate from 02:10Z–03:05Z and can provide request-IDs are eligible for SLA credit consideration.
- Credit estimator (informal):
  Example: If your measured successful requests dropped from 99.9% baseline to 98.5% during the window, estimate lost successful tokens proportionally. We'll follow up with an exact credit calc once tenants provide sample logs.
- To request credit: Reply to this email or open a ticket with a sample of X-Request-Id values and the tenant ID.

FAQ (short):
Q: Was my data exposed?
A: No. This was a routing/capacity issue; no persistent storage or customer payloads were leaked or modified.
Q: Should I change my SDK or client config?
A: No global changes required. If you pin requests to a single EU node, consider using automatic routing for 15 minutes after an event to allow the platform to rebalance.
Q: Will this recur?
A: We've fixed the immediate imbalance and added a monitoring alert to detect similar rollbacks. Root cause action items (below) reduce recurrence risk.

Action items for Redwood (internal checklist, keep in draft):
- [ ] Engineering to finalize postmortem write-up (INF-4572). Owner: Ravi Singh. Due: 2028-08-22.
- [ ] Create retro alert that triggers on control-plane rollback + burst correlation. Owner: Elena Morales. Due: 2028-08-21.
- [ ] Update runbook with two-step rollback verification to avoid partial optimizer state. Owner: Samir Gupta. Due: 2028-08-24.
- [ ] Customer success: send segmented email to pinned-region tenants with instructions (this doc). Owner: Avery Chen. Due: 2028-08-20.

Technical appendix (for customers or SREs who want details):
- Observed metrics: 95th/99th token latency increased ~2x; 429 spike peaked at 0.4% globally, 3.8% for impacted EU edge nodes.
- Logs: X-Request-Id correlation provided in linked ticket.
- PR addressing control-plane guardrails: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1839

Notes to self / copy bank (do not publish as-is):
- Draft short statuspage lines with and without severity label. Pick conservative tone for Monday morning customers.
- Slack threads: #ops, #serving-runtime, #cs-urgent. Paste final statuspage link in each.
- Consider adding a one-line blurb to console alert banner for Dedicated customers.

Contact and escalation:
- Primary contact: Avery Chen (avery@redwood.ai)
- Ops lead: Ravi Singh (ravi@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: pager on INF-4572

End of draft.
